summary: In Citadels, players secretly pick a character role each round (like Assassin, Thief, or King) whose special power shapes the whole round, then use their role to gather gold and build colored city districts. The push is to be the first to build eight districts while out-guessing everyone else's hidden role choices.
praised: Clever hidden-role deduction with real teeth (Assassin/Thief threats)
Quick, light rules for the amount of strategy it delivers
Great player count flexibility and fast turns
High replayability from variable character powers
criticised: Kingmaking possible when players target a leader out of spite
Some character imbalance debated among players
Character abilities can create swingy, sometimes non-interactive rounds
Can run long with more experienced/cutthroat players

interaction.kind: bluffing and take-that via hidden role selection
interaction.detail: Players secretly choose characters whose powers can steal gold, destroy buildings, or kill another player's turn entirely, so deducing who picked what and targeting them is central. Your own city (tableau of districts) is private and separate, but character effects reach directly into opponents' gold and buildings.

win_criteria: Most points, one or two sources

scoring.why: Score is essentially the sum of building costs in your city, with a small number of situational bonuses (completing all colors, being first to eight buildings) layered on top.
scoring.how_you_win: Each round you secretly select a character role for its ability and income, then use gold to construct buildings; once someone reaches seven (or eight) buildings the round finishes and whoever has the highest building-cost total, plus any bonuses, wins.
